title: Songkhla Marathon 2026 Review: The South's Original Marathon Turns 27
seo_title: Songkhla Marathon 2026 Review: Course, Heat & Verdict
meta_description: An honest review of the 27th Songkhla Marathon 2026 in Thailand — flat coastal course, World Athletics label, brutal heat, and who should sign up.
dek: Southern Thailand's longest-running marathon returns to Tinsulanonda Stadium with a World Athletics label behind it — but the August heat is a factor no runner should underestimate.
verdict: Songkhla Marathon is a genuinely historic race — the first marathon in Southern Thailand — now carrying a World Athletics Road Race Label and a flat, seaside, single-loop course past the Gulf of Thailand and Songkhla Lake [1][3]. Organisation is structured, with time-based start blocks and anti-doping oversight, though pickup is in-person only and entries are non-refundable [8]. The real challenge is climate: an August date in a hot, humid province means very early starts are essential [2][6]. It suits runners chasing a scenic, culturally rich Thai race and who respect tropical heat; it's less ideal for anyone hoping for a fast PB attempt.

sections.heading: The Course: Flat, Coastal, and Certified
paragraphs: The headline draw is a single-loop, closed-road course tagged as flat, AIMS-certified and World Athletics Label, running on asphalt with seaside and ocean-view sections <cite index="13-1">flat · Course surface · Road · Other tags · Asphalt · Beach · Beginner Friendly · Bridge · City · Closed Road · Seaside · Family Friendly · Ocean View · Scenic · AIMS certified · Single Loop</cite> [3]. Both the start and finish sit at Tinsulanonda Stadium, and the route is built around <cite index="17-1">stunning views of the Gulf of Thailand and Songkhla Lake</cite> [3]. Race guides also describe a route that runs alongside lakes and ponds before tracing the seashore, giving the marathon a genuinely varied backdrop for a flat course <cite index="3-5">courses that run alongside sparkling lakes and ponds, weave through the bustling city, and trace the seashore</cite> [2].

sections.heading: Conditions: Racing Against the Tropics
paragraphs: This is an August race in a tropical monsoon zone, and organisers clearly plan around it: recent editions have started the marathon around 3:00am, the half around 4:00am, the 10K near 4:45am, with a Saturday-evening fun run the day before [2]. That scheduling matters because <cite index="25-2">temperatures are very warm to hot throughout the year with only minor variation</cite> in Songkhla [6]. Runners flying in from cooler climates should treat heat and humidity, not the flat profile, as the real opponent on race day.

sections.heading: Organisation and Logistics
paragraphs: Songkhla Marathon has real institutional weight behind it: it's <cite index="19-2">recognized as the first marathon race in the South, serving for decades as a prestigious stage that brings together elite runners from Southern Thailand and across the nation</cite>, and in 2023 it <cite index="19-3">entered a new era of pride by achieving the World Athletics Road Race Label</cite> [1]. On the ground, start blocks are assigned by predicted finish time, with priority given to World Athletics- and Thai Athletics-certified runners, and all blocks start simultaneously [8]. The event also runs under formal anti-doping oversight, following the Athletics Integrity Unit's World Athletics rules [8]. Practical friction points worth knowing: bib pickup is in-person only for data-security reasons, and entries are explicitly non-transferable and non-refundable, so plan travel dates around that rigidity [3].

sections.heading: Atmosphere, Field, and the Venue
paragraphs:
The event covers four distances — 5K, 10K, half and full marathon — and has been running since 1999, giving it a longer pedigree than most Thai city races [7]. Community sentiment looks solid, with an 86% recommend rate from reviewers on the race's own Facebook page, though that's from a small sample of just ten reviews [7]. One travel-guide source goes further, claiming 
local participants as well as foreigners compete on the largest monetary award given in Thailand for the winner in a race
 — a claim worth verifying directly with organisers rather than taking at face value [9]. The venue itself, Tinsulanonda Stadium, is a proper 30,000-capacity multi-purpose stadium, though 
just 2,000 of those spaces are covered in a small single-tiered stand along one touchline
 [4]. Not every review of the stadium precinct is glowing — one visitor review calls it 
seriously underused and clearly poorly maintained
, a comment about the surrounding infrastructure rather than the race organisation itself, but worth flagging for anyone expecting a polished big-city venue [5].

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a certified, flat, scenic coastal marathon with genuine local history and you're comfortable racing before dawn in tropical heat, Songkhla delivers on both the course and the credentials [1][3]. It's less suited to first-time international travellers hoping for slick big-race polish everywhere, given the mixed notes on venue upkeep and the strict, non-refundable entry terms [3][5]. For the 2026 27th edition specifically, registration is already closed, so this year's slot is about spectating, volunteering, or locking in the 2027 edition early once entries reopen.

faqs.question: When is the Songkhla Marathon 2026?
faqs.answer: The 27th Songkhla Marathon 2026 takes place on 22-23 August 2026, with a Saturday fun run and the marathon, half marathon and mini marathon held on Sunday, 23 August, starting and finishing at Tinsulanonda Stadium in Songkhla, Thailand.

faqs.question: What distances does the Songkhla Marathon offer?
faqs.answer: The event covers four distances: 5K, 10K, half marathon (21.1km) and full marathon (42.195km), a lineup the race has run since it was established in 1999, making it one of Southern Thailand's longest-standing running events.

faqs.question: Is the Songkhla Marathon course flat?
faqs.answer: Yes. The course is tagged as flat, single-loop, closed-road and AIMS-certified, running on asphalt with seaside sections and views of the Gulf of Thailand and Songkhla Lake around the Tinsulanonda Stadium start/finish area.
